children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Resolves to the platform's default look per context.

children.name: .bordered
children.summary: A tinted platter behind the label.

children.discussion: Reserve it for the one action you most want taken; a screen full of prominent buttons has none.
children.name: .borderedProminent
children.summary: Filled with the tint color — the primary action.

children.name: .plain
children.summary: No chrome until the button is pressed or focused.

children.name: .link
children.summary: Hyperlink styling for navigation-flavored actions (macOS).

discussion: buttonStyle propagates through the environment, so one call on a container restyles every button inside. Built-ins span .plain, .borderless, .bordered, and .borderedProminent; controlSize and tint refine them further.
name: .buttonStyle()
summary: Applies a built-in or custom style to buttons.

children.name: .glass
children.summary: A translucent capsule that lets the content beneath refract through the button.

children.name: .glassProminent
children.summary: A tinted, filled glass capsule reserved for the screen's main call to action.

discussion: WWDC '25 added glass and glassProminent button styles: capsule buttons on the refractive glass material with the system's press morphing. Use them for floating controls above content; inside toolbars, glass comes for free.
name: .buttonStyle(.glass)
summary: Buttons rendered on Liquid Glass material.

children.name: .compact
children.summary: A small inline chip that opens a popover calendar when tapped.

children.name: .graphical
children.summary: Lays out a whole month grid, adding a clock when time is included.

children.name: .wheel
children.summary: Spinning drums per component; available on iOS and watchOS only.

children.name: .field
children.summary: A typed-in text field on macOS; .stepperField adds arrows beside it.

discussion: datePickerStyle spans compact (tap-to-pop-over), graphical (full calendar), wheel on iOS, and field/stepperField on macOS — same binding, very different footprints.
name: .datePickerStyle()
summary: Chooses calendar, wheel, field, or compact date UI.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Reinstates the platform's chevron look inside a custom-styled scope.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: The protocol's sole requirement; return the view that stands in for the whole group.

children.name: DisclosureGroupStyleConfiguration
children.summary: Bundles the label view, the content view, and the isExpanded binding a style drives.

discussion: DisclosureGroupStyle exposes the label, content, and isExpanded binding so you can replace the chevron treatment entirely — animated arrows, plus/minus buttons, or full-row toggles.
name: .disclosureGroupStyle()
summary: Custom expansion chrome for disclosure groups.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Defers to whatever layout the platform normally gives a Form.

children.name: .grouped
children.summary: Rows sit on rounded platters with their labels leading, the Settings-app look.

children.name: .columns
children.summary: Aligns every label in a trailing-justified column beside its control, macOS style.

discussion: formStyle selects grouped (rows on platters, labels leading) or columns (aligned label column, macOS settings look) for a Form. Grouped on macOS gives the iOS-like settings design used since Ventura.
name: .formStyle()
summary: Chooses a form's layout family.

children.name: .linearCapacity
children.summary: A horizontal bar that fills up to the current value, like a storage meter.

children.name: .accessoryLinear
children.summary: A slim track with a marker at the current position, sized for widgets.

children.name: .accessoryCircular
children.summary: An open ring with a marker on the arc and the label centered inside.

children.name: .accessoryCircularCapacity
children.summary: A ring that fills proportionally, ideal for battery-style readouts.

discussion: gaugeStyle spans linear and circular families, including the accessory variants designed for widgets and watch complications where space is tight.
name: .gaugeStyle()
summary: Chooses a gauge's rendering, from bars to dials.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: The stock platter and label placement for the current platform.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Builds the box's chrome around the label and content handed in by the configuration.

children.name: GroupBoxStyleConfiguration
children.summary: Carries just two views, label and content, for the style to arrange.

discussion: A GroupBoxStyle receives the label and content and draws its own platter — brand cards and callout boxes that still read as grouped content at the call site.
name: .groupBoxStyle()
summary: Custom chrome for GroupBox containers.

children.name: .iconOnly
children.summary: Hides the title so only the symbol shows, ideal for cramped toolbars.

children.name: .titleOnly
children.summary: Suppresses the icon where a symbol would just add clutter.

children.name: .titleAndIcon
children.summary: Forces both parts to appear even in contexts that would normally drop one.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Lets each container decide which parts of the label to show.

discussion: labelStyle adapts Labels to their surroundings: iconOnly for compact toolbars, titleOnly where symbols would be noise, titleAndIcon to force both. Custom LabelStyles can rearrange the pair arbitrarily.
name: .labelStyle()
summary: Shows a label's icon, title, or both.

children.name: .plain
children.summary: Edge-to-edge rows with minimal decoration.

children.name: .inset
children.summary: Rows inset from the container's edges.

children.discussion: The standard treatment for the leading column of a NavigationSplitView; section headers gain disclosure behavior automatically.
children.name: .sidebar
children.summary: Source-list styling with collapsible sections.

children.name: .bordered
children.summary: A macOS list framed with a visible border.

discussion: listStyle moves a List between plain, inset, grouped, insetGrouped, and sidebar appearances. Sidebar styling also enables collapsible sections — the standard look for source lists on macOS and iPadOS.
name: .listStyle()
summary: Sets the visual treatment of a list.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Whatever presentation the platform gives a Menu in the current container.

children.name: .button
children.summary: Renders the menu's label as a button that reveals the items when pressed.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Custom MenuStyle hook; rebuild a Menu from the configuration and restyle it.

discussion: menuStyle picks how a Menu presents — the standard button form, or borderlessButton on macOS for toolbar-like menus. Most apps only need it to remove chrome.
name: .menuStyle()
summary: Sets the presentation of menus.

children.name: .menu
children.summary: Collapses the options into a pull-down menu.

children.discussion: Best with two to five short, mutually exclusive options — beyond that the segments get cramped.
children.name: .segmented
children.summary: Every option visible side by side in one control.

children.name: .radioGroup
children.summary: macOS radio buttons, one per option.

children.name: .inline
children.summary: Options listed flat inside the surrounding container.

discussion: pickerStyle switches a Picker between menu, segmented, inline, wheel (iOS), radioGroup (macOS), and palette renderings. The right style depends on option count and how prominent the choice should be.
name: .pickerStyle()
summary: Selects the presentation for pickers.

children.name: .linear
children.summary: A horizontal bar that fills for determinate progress or shimmers when indeterminate.

children.name: .circular
children.summary: A ring that fills to the fraction, or spins when there is no value.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Picks linear or circular depending on the platform and surrounding context.

children.name: makeBody(configuration:)
children.summary: Custom ProgressViewStyle hook; read fractionCompleted from the configuration and draw anything.

discussion: progressViewStyle picks linear or circular rendering independent of whether progress is determinate. A custom ProgressViewStyle reads fractionCompleted from the configuration to draw gauges of any design.
name: .progressViewStyle()
summary: Renders progress as a bar or a circle.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: The platform's default table treatment; inset on macOS.

children.name: .inset
children.summary: Rows pulled in from the edges with no outer frame.

children.name: .bordered
children.summary: Wraps the macOS table in a visible border, the classic Finder-list look.

discussion: tableStyle switches Table between the inset default and bordered variants on macOS, with alternating row backgrounds controlled separately. Mostly a macOS concern; iOS tables keep list styling.
name: .tableStyle()
summary: Adjusts a table's borders and row insets.

children.name: .page(indexDisplayMode:)
children.summary: Turns tabs into horizontally swipeable pages and controls the dot indicator; not on macOS.

children.name: .sidebarAdaptable
children.summary: A tab bar that can expand into a sidebar on iPad and Mac, with sections becoming groups.

children.name: .tabBarOnly
children.summary: Pins the tabs to a bar and never promotes them into a sidebar.

children.name: .grouped
children.summary: macOS-only style that lays the tabs out as a segmented control above the content.

discussion: tabViewStyle turns a TabView into swipeable pages (page), the watch's vertical carousel, or sidebarAdaptable (2024) where tabs can promote into a sidebar on iPad and Mac.
name: .tabViewStyle()
summary: Switches tabs between bar, page, and sidebar modes.

children.name: .plain
children.summary: Strips all chrome, the starting point for a fully custom field design.

children.name: .roundedBorder
children.summary: A rounded outline around the field, the familiar form-entry appearance.

children.name: .squareBorder
children.summary: A crisp rectangular frame available only on macOS.

children.name: .automatic
children.summary: Whatever the surrounding container would give a text field by default.

discussion: textFieldStyle switches between plain, roundedBorder, and the macOS squareBorder appearance for every field in scope. Plain is the base for fully custom field designs built with background and overlay.
name: .textFieldStyle()
summary: Chooses how text fields draw their chrome.

children.name: .switch
children.summary: The sliding on/off switch.

children.name: .checkbox
children.summary: The classic macOS checkbox.

children.discussion: The natural fit for formatting toggles — bold, italic, filters — especially with a symbol label in a toolbar.
children.name: .button
children.summary: A button that stays highlighted while on.

discussion: The same Toggle declaration can appear as an iOS switch, a macOS checkbox, or a pressed-state button via .button style. Custom ToggleStyle conformances take over rendering entirely.
name: .toggleStyle()
summary: Chooses how toggles render — switch, checkbox, or button.

children.name: AngularGradient(colors:center:startAngle:endAngle:)
children.summary: Spreads an evenly spaced color list around the center between two angles.

children.name: AngularGradient(gradient:center:angle:)
children.summary: The conic form: a full sweep from a Gradient, rotated by a single angle.

children.code:
AngularGradient(
    stops: [
        .init(color: .green, location: 0),
        .init(color: .green, location: 0.7),
        .init(color: .red, location: 0.7),
        .init(color: .red, location: 1)
    ],
    center: .center, startAngle: .zero, endAngle: .degrees(270)
)
children.name: AngularGradient(stops:center:startAngle:endAngle:)
children.summary: Positions each color at an explicit location along the arc via Gradient.Stop values.

children.name: .conicGradient(colors:center:angle:)
children.summary: The ShapeStyle shorthand that builds the same sweep without naming the type.

discussion: AngularGradient (a conic gradient) rotates through its stops around a center, from a start to an end angle — the foundation of color wheels and circular meters.
name: AngularGradient
summary: Sweeps colors around a center point.

children.name: timingCurve(_:_:_:_:duration:)
children.summary: Four raw Bézier coordinates, the same numbers a CSS cubic-bezier takes.

children.name: timingCurve(_:duration:)
children.summary: Drives the animation with a UnitCurve, so presets and custom curves share one API.

children.name: UnitCurve.bezier(startControlPoint:endControlPoint:)
children.summary: Builds a reusable cubic curve from two control points that you can also sample directly.

discussion: timingCurve defines an animation's pacing as a cubic Bézier: two control points bend the time-versus-progress curve between a standing start and a full stop. easeIn, easeOut, and easeInOut are all presets of this one function. Drag the control points in the demo and replay to feel how the curve's shape becomes motion.
name: Animation.timingCurve()
summary: A cubic Bézier timing curve for animations.

children.code:
let pressed = Color.accentColor.mix(with: .black, by: 0.15)
let raw = Color.red.mix(with: .blue, by: 0.5, in: .device)
children.name: mix(with:by:in:)
children.summary: Interpolates toward another color by a 0–1 fraction, optionally in the device color space.

children.code:
Rectangle()
    .fill(Color.yellow.mix(with: .blue, by: 0.5, in: .perceptual))
Rectangle()
    .fill(Color.yellow.mix(with: .blue, by: 0.5, in: .device))
children.name: Gradient.ColorSpace
children.summary: Chooses between perceptual blending, which avoids muddy midpoints, and raw device math.

discussion: A WWDC '24 addition: mix interpolates a color toward another by a given fraction, in perceptual or device color spaces — no more manual component math for hover tints and charts.
name: Color.mix()
summary: Blends two colors by a fraction in a color space.

children.name: ImagePaint(image:sourceRect:scale:)
children.summary: Tiles an image, cropped to a unit-space rectangle and scaled, as a paint.

children.name: .image(_:sourceRect:scale:)
children.summary: The ShapeStyle static that produces the same tiled fill inline.

discussion: ImagePaint repeats a source image (or a cropped portion) as a ShapeStyle — textured fills and patterned borders without a custom shader.
name: ImagePaint
summary: Tiles an image as a fill or stroke style.

children.name: LinearGradient(colors:startPoint:endPoint:)
children.summary: Spaces a color list evenly between two unit points.

children.code:
let brand = Gradient(colors: [.indigo, .pink])

Rectangle()
    .fill(LinearGradient(gradient: brand,
                         startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing))
children.name: LinearGradient(gradient:startPoint:endPoint:)
children.summary: Takes a prebuilt Gradient, letting you reuse one stop list across several fills.

children.code:
LinearGradient(
    stops: [
        .init(color: .black, location: 0),
        .init(color: .black.opacity(0), location: 0.4)
    ],
    startPoint: .bottom, endPoint: .top
)
children.name: LinearGradient(stops:startPoint:endPoint:)
children.summary: Pins each color to an explicit location for hard edges or uneven fades.

children.name: .linearGradient(colors:startPoint:endPoint:)
children.summary: The ShapeStyle shorthand for use anywhere a style is expected, such as foregroundStyle.

discussion: LinearGradient interpolates between color stops from a start to an end unit point. As a ShapeStyle it slots into fill, background, and foregroundStyle alike; every Color also offers a subtle built-in .gradient variant.
name: LinearGradient
summary: Blends colors along a straight line.

children.name: .ultraThinMaterial
children.summary: The lightest blur, letting most of the backdrop's color and shape through.

children.name: .regularMaterial
children.summary: The middle weight that balances legibility with a sense of the content behind.

children.name: .ultraThickMaterial
children.summary: The most opaque material, nearly a solid surface with a hint of blur.

children.name: .bar
children.summary: Matches the material system toolbars and tab bars use.

discussion: Materials — ultraThin through ultraThick, plus bar — blur whatever is behind them and keep vibrant text legible on top. They are ShapeStyles, so they slot into background and fill; under the 2025 design language, glassEffect supersedes them for floating controls.
name: Material
summary: Translucent blur layers that adapt to their backdrop.

children.code:
MeshGradient(
    width: 2, height: 2,
    points: [[0, 0], [1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]],
    colors: [.red, .orange, .purple, .blue],
    smoothsColors: false
)
children.name: MeshGradient(width:height:points:colors:background:smoothsColors:colorSpace:)
children.summary: The direct form: a grid of unit-space points and a matching flat array of colors.

children.code:
MeshGradient(
    width: 2, height: 2,
    locations: .points([[0, 0], [1, 0], [0, 1], [1, 1]]),
    colors: .colors([.mint, .teal, .indigo, .cyan]),
    background: .black,
    colorSpace: .perceptual
)
children.name: MeshGradient(width:height:locations:colors:background:smoothsColors:colorSpace:)
children.summary: The general form that accepts Bézier control points and pre-resolved colors.

children.code:
let simple: MeshGradient.Locations = .points(grid)
let curved: MeshGradient.Locations = .bezierPoints(bezierGrid)
children.name: MeshGradient.Locations
children.summary: Either plain points or full BezierPoints describing how the mesh cells curve.

children.code:
let corner = MeshGradient.BezierPoint(
    position: [0, 0],
    leadingControlPoint: [0, 0],
    topControlPoint: [0, 0],
    trailingControlPoint: [0.3, 0],
    bottomControlPoint: [0, 0.3]
)
children.name: MeshGradient.BezierPoint
children.summary: A vertex plus four control handles that bend the edges meeting at it.

discussion: New at WWDC '24, MeshGradient interpolates colors across a grid of movable control points, producing fluid, organic blends impossible with linear or radial gradients. Animate the points for lava-lamp backgrounds.
name: MeshGradient
summary: A 2D mesh of control points, each with its own color.

children.name: RadialGradient(colors:center:startRadius:endRadius:)
children.summary: Fades an evenly spaced color list from an inner to an outer radius in points.

children.code:
let glow = Gradient(colors: [.white, .clear])

Circle()
    .fill(RadialGradient(gradient: glow, center: .topLeading,
                         startRadius: 0, endRadius: 120))
children.name: RadialGradient(gradient:center:startRadius:endRadius:)
children.summary: Builds the same glow from a reusable Gradient value.

children.code:
RadialGradient(
    stops: [
        .init(color: .white, location: 0),
        .init(color: .white, location: 0.2),
        .init(color: .blue, location: 0.25)
    ],
    center: .center, startRadius: 0, endRadius: 80
)
children.name: RadialGradient(stops:center:startRadius:endRadius:)
children.summary: Explicit stop locations produce sharp rings or a tight highlight.

children.name: .radialGradient(colors:center:startRadius:endRadius:)
children.summary: The ShapeStyle shorthand for backgrounds and strokes without naming the type.

discussion: RadialGradient runs its stops from a center unit point between a start and end radius — the go-to for spotlight and glow effects.
name: RadialGradient
summary: Blends colors outward from a center point.
